Settings.MerchantBound: double-clicking their token opens this window
Settings.MerchantNoAccess: Players have no access to this actor, so double-clicking the token does nothing for them.
Settings.MerchantHint: Their name and portrait are used below unless you override them. Pair this with turning off “players can open the window themselves” and the only way in is to visit them.
Settings.DragActorHint: gives the party somewhere to go to trade
Settings.HostImgEg: an icon above, or browse for artwork
Settings.HostIconHint: Pick an icon, or browse for your own portrait art.
Settings.ResourcesHint: One is plenty for most tables. Add more and every upgrade can be priced in any combination of them, so something might cost 3 Marks and 1 Favor.
Settings.IconHint: Pick one above, or browse for your own image.
Settings.WorthOne: one of these is worth one {currency}
Settings.DragItemHint: lets you hide payment in a chest for the party to loot
Settings.AutoDeposit: Credit it the moment a player picks it up
Settings.AutoDepositHint: Leave it unticked and players hand the currency in with a button in this window instead.
Settings.PlayersCanOpen: Players can open the window themselves
Settings.SampleFlavor1: Costly to make, and worth every coin.
Settings.SampleFlavor2: Salvaged, repaired, and better than it began.
Settings.SampleHint: Sample content. Your own upgrades and art replace it.
Settings.NoGroupActor: This world has no Group actor yet, so party-wide upgrades would go to all {count} player-owned characters, chests and wildshape copies included. Create a Group actor with just your player characters and pick it here.
Settings.NoPartyActor: Without a party actor, party-wide upgrades apply to all {count} player-owned characters, which usually includes actors you did not mean.

Shop.TierGate: Take {count} more in the rows above
Shop.EffectSecret: Its effect is not yet known
Shop.EffectSecretDetail: Its effect is not yet known. It is revealed once taken.
Shop.Empty: Nothing on offer yet… (GM: add upgrades via “Manage”.)
Shop.ClickHint: Click a card to inspect it
Shop.MysteryFlavor: “Prove yourselves further, and I may show you more…”

Editor.ResyncHint: Re-create any missing granted effects on their current targets (late joiners, roster changes, hand-deleted effects)
Editor.PlaceHint: Put currency into a chest or an NPC for the party to find
Editor.NoSections: No sections yet. Upgrades show as one flat list until you add some.
Editor.OrphanTitle: The item this was bought for no longer exists, or nobody carries it. Refund the purchase, or point the upgrade at a new item.
Editor.GateWarn: Row {row} can never open: exclusive choices cap what the rows above can supply. Lower the gate or add talents.
Editor.NoUpgrades: No upgrades yet. Create your first one.
Editor.ClearHint: Remove lines from the history. Balances and owned upgrades stay as they are.
Editor.RemoveLine: Remove this line from the log
Editor.Title: Upgrade Board: GM Console

UpgradeEditor.Name: Name
UpgradeEditor.FlavorEg: Worn smooth by years of use.
UpgradeEditor.ComesAfterHint: Tick anything that must be owned before this can be bought. It stays visible but locked until then, and the two are shown as linked.
UpgradeEditor.CannotTakeWithHint: Tick anything the party must choose between. Buying one rules out the others, and a refund opens the choice again. Ticking it on one side is enough.
UpgradeEditor.Repeatable: Can be bought more than once
UpgradeEditor.BuyerHint: Decided at purchase: the player's own character, or whoever the GM picks when the GM buys it. Combine with “Can be bought more than once” for something each character gets separately, like an item.
UpgradeEditor.NoTargetWarn: Pick a character, or the effect will not apply to anyone.
UpgradeEditor.BuilderUnsupported: The bonus builder ships presets for dnd5e and PF2e. In {system} you can still add custom targets below, or link an existing effect instead.
UpgradeEditor.PresetTitle: Choose what this bonus applies to
UpgradeEditor.BonusTypeTitle: PF2e counts only the highest bonus of each type
UpgradeEditor.Pf2eDice: Enter a flat number like 1, or dice like 1d6. Extra dice have no bonus type, so that dropdown disappears when you type dice.
UpgradeEditor.Pf2eWhyType: Why the type matters: PF2e adds only the largest bonus of each type. Two item bonuses to AC do not become +2. The bigger one simply wins.
UpgradeEditor.Pf2eUntyped: If you only want it to work and do not care about the math, pick Untyped.
UpgradeEditor.Dnd5eFormula: Give each value a sign: +2 for a flat bonus, +1d8[cold] for extra dice of a damage type. If you leave the sign off, it is added for you. Ability scores and darkvision are plain numbers, so write 2 or 60.
UpgradeEditor.DragEffect: Drag an Effect or Item here
UpgradeEditor.DragEffectHint: from a character sheet, the Items sidebar, or a compendium
UpgradeEditor.DragItemHint: from a character sheet. The upgrade goes on that exact item.
UpgradeEditor.ItemUnresolved: The chosen item no longer exists. Drop a new one here.
UpgradeEditor.ItemUnowned: Nobody carries this item any more, so its effect reaches no one until someone picks it up.
UpgradeEditor.ItemTargetHint: The effect travels with the item and applies to whoever has it equipped (and attuned or invested, where the system asks for it). A stashed item grants nothing.
UpgradeEditor.ItemChoiceNote: The buyer picks the item at purchase. Leave the drop zone empty for that, or set a fixed item here to skip the question.
UpgradeEditor.UuidEg: filled in by dragging, or paste one
UpgradeEditor.UuidUnresolved: Nothing in this world matches that UUID.
UpgradeEditor.ShowInEffectsBar: Show it in the effects bar
UpgradeEditor.KeepSecret: Keep what it does secret until it is owned
UpgradeEditor.Nominate: Have them nominate something when they buy this
UpgradeEditor.Question: Question
UpgradeEditor.GuidanceEg: Drag a spell from your spellbook.
UpgradeEditor.ChoiceHint: A window opens before the cost is paid, and canceling it buys nothing. The answer names the granted item, like “Temporary Scroll (Fireball)”, and is linked in its description.

Layout.Label: Layout
Layout.Rows: Rows: a flat list of cards
Layout.Tree: Talent tree: a grid with connecting arrows
Layout.Hint: A talent tree draws upgrades as tiles, with arrows along the “comes after” links. Prerequisites then stay within the section.
Layout.GateHint: With 2, the second row opens once 2 different talents above it are taken, the third once 4 are. A talent bought twice counts once. 0 turns this off. Talent trees only.
Layout.BackgroundHint: Panel art drawn behind a talent tree, dimmed so the tiles stay readable. Leave empty for the plain panel.

Arrange.Title: Arrange: {section}
Arrange.Hint: Drag a tile onto a cell to pin it there. Pinned tiles keep their place when the links change; clearing the pin hands the tile back to automatic placement.

Dnd5e.spell_damage_all: All spell damage (incl. saving throw spells)
Dnd5e.item_magic: Magical bonus (attack and damage; AC on armor)
Dnd5e.item_damage: Extra damage dealt by this item

Pf2e.rune_potency: Potency rune (attack, or AC on armor)

BonusType.circumstance: Circumstance: from where you are or what you did
BonusType.circumstanceHint: Terrain, cover, a lit beacon, a clever plan. The usual choice for something the world provides.
BonusType.item: Item: from gear, a rune, an installed upgrade
BonusType.itemHint: Will not stack with a magic weapon or armor giving the same kind of bonus. The larger one wins.
BonusType.status: Status: from a spell, condition or blessing
BonusType.statusHint: Will not stack with spell buffs like Bless that grant the same kind of bonus.
BonusType.untypedHint: Nothing suppresses it. Use it when you just want the bonus to apply, at the cost of breaking PF2e's stacking math.
BonusType.proficiencyHint: Reserved for training rank. Almost never what an upgrade should grant.
BonusType.abilityHint: Reserved for an attribute modifier. Almost never what an upgrade should grant.

Setting.PlayersCanOpen: Players can open the window freely
Setting.AutoDeposit: Credit currency automatically when picked up

SettingHint.ActionVerb: The label on the purchase button. E.g. “Buy”, “Request”, “Claim”.
SettingHint.CurrencyIcon: A Font Awesome class (e.g. “fa-solid fa-seedling”) or a path to an image in your Foundry data folder.
SettingHint.CurrencyItem: An Item representing one unit, so the currency can be looted from a chest or a body.
SettingHint.CurrencyName: The resource that is spent. E.g. “Marks”.
SettingHint.HostActor: Double-clicking this actor's token opens the window, so the party has somewhere to go.
SettingHint.HostImg: Path to an image in your Foundry data folder. Leave empty for a default icon.
SettingHint.HostName: The NPC or place presenting the upgrades. E.g. “The Quartermaster”.
SettingHint.PartyActor: The Group (dnd5e) or Party (PF2e) actor whose members receive party-wide upgrades. Set this: without it they go to every player-owned character, chests and wildshape copies included.
SettingHint.PlayersCanOpen: If disabled, players only see it when the GM shows it to them.
SettingHint.RequireApproval: If enabled, player purchase requests must be approved by the GM before the cost is deducted.
SettingHint.Theme: Color and texture of the player-facing window.
SettingHint.WindowTitle: Shown in the window title bar. E.g. “The Exchange”.

Menu.Name: Upgrade Board setup
Menu.Label: Open setup
Menu.Hint: Theme, wording, currency icon, party actor and purchase rules, with a live preview.

Refuse.Unavailable: That upgrade is no longer available.
Refuse.TierGate: “{name}” opens once {count} more of the talents above it are taken.
Refuse.NoItemChosen: “{name}” needs a carried item nominated with the purchase.
Refuse.RuledOut: “{name}” is ruled out because “{rival}” was chosen instead.
Refuse.NoCharacterChosen: No character chosen, so nothing was purchased.
Refuse.NoAssignedCharacter: You have no assigned character, so this cannot be granted. Ask your GM.
Refuse.TargetGone: “{name}” cannot be bought: its character or item no longer exists. Nothing was spent.

EffectMode.Link: Use an existing effect or item

Exclusive.OnlyOne: Only one of this and {names} can ever be taken.
Exclusive.PulledOne: {names} is part of this choice too, through one of the upgrades ticked here.
Exclusive.PulledMany: {names} are part of this choice too, through the upgrades ticked here.

PartyNote.Configured: Party membership comes from “{name}” ({count} member(s)), set in module settings.
PartyNote.Fallback: No party actor is set in module settings, so this goes to all {count} player-owned character(s). Set one before using party-wide upgrades.

GrantNote.Pf2eEffect: Granted as an Effect, so it sits in the effects bar
GrantNote.ActiveEffect: Granted as an Active Effect, so it sits on the Effects tab
GrantNote.QuietFeature: Granted as a quiet, permanent feature on the sheet
GrantNote.OnItem: Placed on the item itself, applying to whoever has it equipped
GrantNote.Sentence: {how}; removing or refunding the upgrade deletes it again.
GrantNote.AlreadyOwned: This upgrade is already owned. Saving applies it to its targets again.

Dialog.DeleteUpgradeOwned: It is currently owned, so its effect will also be removed from every character that has it.
Dialog.RefundBody: Refund {name}? This returns {price} and removes its effect from {who}.
Dialog.RefundRemaining: {count} other acquisition(s) of this upgrade are left untouched.
Dialog.DeleteSectionKeeps: Its {count} upgrade(s) are kept and simply become uncategorized.
Dialog.ClearHistoryBody: This only removes lines from the history. No {currency} moves and no purchase is undone.
Dialog.EditReasonNote: Only the reason can be changed. The amount stays as it is.
Dialog.RemoveResourceNote: Its balance is discarded, and any upgrade priced in it stops costing it.

Notify.NoPartyMembers: Upgrade Board: there are no party members to grant this to. Set a Party actor in Setup.
Notify.EffectFailed: Upgrade Board: acquired, but the effect could not be applied automatically.
Notify.NoGM: Upgrade Board: no GM is connected right now. Try again when one is.
Notify.NoCurrencyItem: Upgrade Board: no currency item is set. Choose one in Setup.
Notify.NoCurrencyItemSetup: Upgrade Board: choose a currency item in Setup first.
Notify.EmptyDrop: Upgrade Board: nothing usable was dropped there.
Notify.ShownToPlayers: “{title}” has been shown to all players.
Notify.LinkUnresolved: Upgrade Board: the linked effect for “{name}” could not be found.
Notify.NoTarget: Upgrade Board: “{name}” has no valid target to apply its effect to.
Notify.ApplyFailed: Upgrade Board: failed to apply “{name}” to {actor}. The console has the details.
Notify.RemovedGrants: Upgrade Board: removed {count} granted item(s) and effect(s) from character sheets.
Notify.Resynced: Upgrade Board: re-sync complete ({count} created, {refreshed} brought up to date).
Notify.NeedOneResource: Upgrade Board: there has to be at least one resource.
Notify.MerchantAccessGranted: Upgrade Board: players can now interact with the merchant's token.
Notify.PickACharacter: Upgrade Board: pick a character for a single-character upgrade.
Notify.PickAnItem: Upgrade Board: pick an item for an item upgrade.
Notify.ItemNeedsOwner: Upgrade Board: nobody carries that item. Drag it from a character sheet instead.
Notify.ItemLinkUnsupported: Upgrade Board: “{name}” links something an item cannot carry. Build the effect instead, or link an Active Effect.
Notify.NoMagicField: Upgrade Board: “{item}” cannot carry a magical bonus. Only a weapon, armor or ammunition can.
Notify.RuneWrongItemType: Upgrade Board: “{item}” is the wrong kind of item for “{label}”.
Notify.RuneAlready: Upgrade Board: “{item}” already carries that property rune.
Notify.RuneNotBetter: Upgrade Board: “{item}” already has a rune at least that strong, so nothing was added.
Notify.RuneAbp: Upgrade Board: this world uses Automatic Bonus Progression, which overrides rune values. The rune was recorded but will not apply.
Notify.RuneNeedsPotency: Upgrade Board: “{item}” carries more property runes than its potency has slots for; the extra stays dormant until the potency rises.
Notify.RuneChangedByHand: Upgrade Board: a rune on “{item}” was changed by hand after this purchase, so that value was left as it is.
Notify.ItemRowsDropped: Upgrade Board: this upgrade no longer targets an item, so its item-only bonus rows were removed.
Notify.Migrated: Upgrade Board: your existing board came across from the older “Upgrades” module ({count} upgrades). You can safely disable that one now.
